scenes.title: 1987 Trinity University Booth: Hand Hovering Then Slamming the Chrome Tap-Bell Past 16 Rebound Rings
scenes.era: 1987, Trinity University individual recording booth, San Antonio, Texas

layout.description: Sunlit 1987 acoustic testing room with warm oak desk, gleaming chrome call-bell, stand microphone, bold tabletop placard reading 'DO NOT THINK OF A WHITE BEAR', and an observation window where Daniel Wegner tracks bell counts climbing from 6 to 16.

positions.who: 42-year-old adult volunteer in crisp 1987 collared knit polo and slacks
positions.where: seated upright at the oak booth desk with right palm poised tense above the chrome tap-bell before striking it down
positions.facing: facing the chrome desk bell and stand microphone

positions.who: Daniel Wegner in 1987 Oxford button-down shirt and tortoiseshell glasses
positions.where: standing at the observation window clicking a mechanical tally counter as Period-2 rings pass 16
positions.facing: observing the volunteer's desk bell through glass

props.name: gleaming chrome tabletop tap-bell beside stand microphone
props.period_detail: classic 1987 spring-loaded silver call bell centered on the oak recording desk
props.physical_behavior: State-A palm hovers tense 5 cm above dome -> State-B palm strikes bell dome down with crisp metallic ring (>6 rings in Period 1, 16 rings in Period 2)

props.name: printed 'DO NOT THINK OF A WHITE BEAR' desk placard and mechanical tally counter
props.period_detail: bold black-on-cream 1987 instruction card paired with researcher's handheld click counter
props.physical_behavior: State-A volunteer flips Period-2 card over -> State-B researcher clicks silver tally counter rapidly up to 16 rebound rings

actions.verb_sequence: holds right hand tense above the chrome bell trying to focus on the desk lamp -> winces as a white bear intrudes -> strikes palm firmly onto the silver tap-bell -> shakes head and strikes the bell again
flips the Period-2 window card to 'Express Freely' -> clicks handheld counter up to 16 rings

reactions.reaction: exhales a wry, rueful laugh realizing fighting the thought made the bell ring nonstop
records the 16-vs-12 rebound spike on his clipboard

scenes.wardrobe: 1987 smart-casual adult attire: navy cotton knit polo and khaki trousers; researcher in striped Oxford shirt.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key 1987 laboratory daylight through tall acoustic-room windows.
scenes.recognition_hook: Ordered NOT to picture a white bear for five minutes, volunteers keep slamming a silver desk bell every forty-five seconds — then rebound to sixteen rings once the ban lifts.

key_visual.description: an adult volunteer in a sunlit 1987 testing booth striking a chrome desk tap-bell beside a stand microphone and a 'DO NOT THINK OF A WHITE BEAR' card while Daniel Wegner clicks a tally counter

scenes.title: 3 A.M. Adult Bedroom Spiral: Fighting the Clock Doubles Wakefulness
scenes.era: Modern suburban master bedroom at 3:00 a.m.

layout.description: Cool moonlit master bedroom where a tired 48-year-old homeowner sits upright beside a glowing bedside clock, flipping the clock face-down while trying to force sleep.

positions.where: sitting up against pillows turning the bedside alarm clock away in frustration

props.name: bedside alarm clock and notepad
props.period_detail: modern warm-amber nightstand clock beside a legal pad
props.physical_behavior: State-A hand grips glowing clock -> State-B turns clock face-down yet eyes snap wide open

actions.verb_sequence: squeezes eyes shut commanding 'Stop thinking about the 8 a.m. meeting' -> snaps wide awake

reactions.reaction: rubs temples recognizing blunt thought suppression backfired

scenes.lighting: Crisp cool moonlight balanced with warm bedside lamp rim light.
scenes.recognition_hook: Commanding your brain 'Stop worrying and sleep!' at 3 a.m. feeds the exact radar keeping you awake.

scenes.title: Experiment 2 Antidote: One Red Die-Cast Volkswagen Silences the Bell

layout.description: Same oak testing desk, now featuring a bright red die-cast Volkswagen Beetle model placed squarely in front of the untouched, silent chrome tap-bell.

positions.where: seated calmly rolling the small red Volkswagen model across the desk while the silver bell stays untouched
positions.facing: facing the red Volkswagen model and microphone

props.name: red die-cast Volkswagen Beetle model beside silent chrome tap-bell
props.period_detail: 1980s miniature red Beetle used to stage Wegner's Experiment 2 focused-distraction cure
props.physical_behavior: State-A hand reaches past bell -> State-B fingers roll red Beetle smoothly forward while bell stays completely silent

actions.verb_sequence: picks up the single red Volkswagen focus -> speaks calmly into mic with zero rebound bell rings

reactions.reaction: nods with calm relief as the rebound surge vanishes

scenes.recognition_hook: Giving a tired mind ONE concrete replacement destination wiped out the white-bear rebound completely.

scenes.title: Outdoor Morning Putting Green: Aiming at the Center Flagstick Instead of the Pond
scenes.era: Modern sunlit morning neighborhood golf green (Outdoor)

layout.description: Open-air sunlit morning putting green beside a sparkling pond where a 55-year-old golfer aligns putter squarely toward the crisp white center pin and rolls the ball straight into the cup.

positions.who: 55-year-old golfer in breathable polo shirt and chinos
positions.where: standing on the sunlit outdoor green pointing putter blade at the center flagstick before striking a clean putt

props.name: brass putter, white golf ball, and center flagstick beside pond
props.period_detail: classic outdoor weekend golf green setup
props.physical_behavior: State-A golfer grounds putter behind white ball -> State-B smooth pendulum stroke rolls ball dead-center into cup

actions.verb_sequence: locks gaze onto a single spot on the cup -> strokes ball smoothly into the hole

scenes.wardrobe: Light sage golf polo, tailored chinos, walking shoes.
scenes.lighting: Crisp golden outdoor morning sunlight across green turf.
scenes.recognition_hook: Feed your brain the exact target you want — never the water hazard you fear.
